title: Orbital Angular Momentum Transfer and Beam-Quality Limits in Fork-Grating Electron Diffraction
authors: P. K. Tsiopa, S. S. Baturin
abstract: We analyze fork-grating generation of electron vortex beams beyond the ideal single-mode approximation. The incident beam is described as a paraxial Gaussian ensemble with finite transverse momentum spread and a first electromagnetic Hartree phase accumulated before the grating. Within Fresnel propagation we derive an analytical expression for each diffraction order and determine the corresponding orbital-angular-momentum statistics. The mean OAM of a selected order remains fixed by the topological rule, $\langle L_z\rangle_m=mp\hbar$, while its variance is set by the residual transverse momentum spread of the beam prepared at the grating. For the Gaussian mixture, the transverse purity is $\mathcal P_{\perp,m}=[1+2(ΔL_{z,m}/\hbar)^2]^{-1}$. The observed annular profile is governed by a separate propagation-dependent blurring scale, so a beam can retain well-defined mean OAM while having low transverse purity or a partially filled vortex minimum. Within the radial phase-screen approximation, the Hartree self-field modifies the propagated profile while preserving the full-plane OAM moments and transverse purity.
summary: This theoretical work investigates how Orbital Angular Momentum is transferred and limited when electron beams diffract through a fork-grating structure. By incorporating the effects of an electromagnetic self-field, the authors show that while the mean OAM is topologically protected, the beam's transverse purity is limited by the initial transverse momentum spread. The methodology combines relativistic quantum mechanics with advanced diffraction theory.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the transfer of Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) and the resulting beam-quality limits when electron vortex beams diffract through a fork-grating structure.
main_result: The mean OAM ($\langle L_z angle_m$) is robustly fixed by the topological rule ($m\hbar$), while the beam's transverse purity is determined by the residual transverse momentum spread ($\Delta L_{z,m}$).
method: The analysis uses a paraxial approximation, incorporating an electromagnetic Hartree self-field phase screen into the Fresnel propagation kernel to model the diffraction process.
model_or_system: The system involves an electron ensemble propagating through a region where it accumulates a Hartree self-field phase before diffracting through a holographic fork-grating. The description uses a modified Schrödinger-like equation derived from relativistic considerations.
key_observables: Mean OAM ($\langle L_z angle_m$), Transverse Purity ($P_{\perp,m}$), and OAM Variance ($\Delta L_{z,m}$).
important_parameters: The residual transverse momentum spread ($\Delta L_{z,m}$), the grating period ($D$), and the accumulated Hartree phase ($	ilde{\chi}_{em}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the quasistatic electromagnetic Hartree approximation and assumes a phase-screen model for propagation, neglecting higher-order self-field corrections.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometry of the fork-grating setup, including the compensation of deterministic transverse momentum, and show the displacement of the single-component beam.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general description of the electron ensemble and the Hartree potential, derives the order-resolved field using Bessel functions, and finally calculates the OAM variance using Hankel transforms and closure relations.
why_interesting: It provides a detailed theoretical framework for quantifying fundamental quantum beam properties (OAM) in structured matter-wave optics, connecting topological invariants to measurable beam quality metrics like purity.

The blue and red curves correspond to kx = 0 and kx = 107 m−1, respectively, with ky = 0, at z −ζ = 3 mm in the low-density regime described in the text. The profiles of Eq. FIG. 3. Effect of incoherent transverse-momentum averaging on the observed diffraction profile for m = 1 at z −ζ = 3 mm, with negligible Hartree correction. The blue curve is the centered component kx = ky = 0; the red curve is the ensemble profile of Eq. (34) for the Gaussian distribution in Eq. (19), with σk = 107 m−1. Both curves are line profiles along the positive x axis, with ρ0 = ρ and θ0 = θ = 0. Averaging over the displaced component centers fills the intensity minimum at the mean beam center and smooths the radial oscillations.

FIG. 4. Diffraction profiles including the common radial electromagnetic Hartree phase for m = 1 of Eq. (17), at z−ζ = 3 mm. The blue curve represents the centered component kx = ky = 0; the red curve represents the incoherent Gaussian ensemble with σk = 107 m−1. The curves are plotted along the positive x axis, using ρ0 = ρ and θ0 = θ = 0. The broader radial structure compared with Fig. 3 illustrates the defocusing action of the Hartree phase. The scale ρc in Eq. (35) characterizes the exponential branch of the solution. This common radial phase preserves the full-plane OAM moments and transverse-state purity. The concentration for this figure is taken as n = 1018m−3 and ˜χem ≈1.5 × 1014.
